full_judgment: 4. Mr. Khondker has referred to certain decisions in support of his contention that where statute provides adequate protection, injunction should not be issued. He has referred to the case of Mati Lail Pal v. Priya Nath Mitra (1). In this case it was held that the doctrine of lies pendent applies in a case of specific performance of a contract. In the case of Johar Lal Bhutra v. Bhupendra Nath Basu (2) it was held—"When a suit for specific performance of a contract for transfer of immovable property is ended by a final decree transferring the title, that title relates back to the date of the agreement on which the suit is based and the Court will not permit its decree to be rendered nugatory by intermediate conveyances."
